host_key_verified: SHA256:CIaC5hU5v0pJGNKj5M5uxg7zZrecCuoRRB69v7x65/Q, matching the fingerprint recorded in SAT-BACKUP on 2026-08-31 while the machine was under our control
coexistence: The machine already runs satledger behind Caddy on 80/443. ufw was already active with those ports allowed, and provision.sh only ADDS rules rather than resetting them, so both survived. Verified after provisioning: 80 returns 308 (Caddy's HTTPS redirect) and 443 returns 400 (curl without SNI) -- both alive.
tooling_gap_found: provision.sh writes no outbound peer. It stands a node up as THE seed, not as one joining an existing network, so the node came up at height 0 with only the genesis it minted itself -- listening, but with nothing to serve. The cross-check timed out, which looks like a network fault and is not one. Fixed by adding --connect to the systemd unit; the runbook now carries the step.
what_this_buys: Availability. Two providers, two jurisdictions, two failure domains. NOT operator independence -- both seeds are ours, and a reader who distrusts this project gains nothing from a second machine the same project runs.
remaining: DNS (seed2.bitcoin-lab.org), and a third seed on a third provider, ideally outside the operator's own jurisdiction, which is the part that begins to buy more than uptime.
